locators.claim: Double braiding defines a homomorphism from invertible objects to tensor automorphisms of the identity; its kernel consists of transparent invertible objects, and it is an isomorphism when the braided fusion category is nondegenerate.

For the fully symmetric special case C=Rep(G), the stated Crane-Yetter normalization is identified with a count of flat G-connections; a flat connection is described through a homomorphism from pi1 to G.

For arbitrary ribbon fusion category input, the ordinary Crane-Yetter-Kauffman theory is not sensitive to exotic smooth structure; transparent fermions are tied to vanishing Gauss sums.

scope: Primary-source locators used to red-team the proposed premodular Twisted Yetter sector/quadratic ansatz and to delimit what is and is not source-backed.
scope_guardrails: No source in this ledger proves the proposed homologically twisted premodular closed formula.
The Bärenz-Barrett flat-connection result is a fully symmetric Rep(G) special case and is not a sector-decomposition theorem for every premodular category.
Reutter concerns ordinary semisimple four-dimensional TFT and ordinary Crane-Yetter-Kauffman values, not the alpha-marked Yetter formula proposed here.
Tham's premodular handle maps warn that unsimplified categorical projection data may remain; they do not imply a scalar sector sum.
Yetter's introductory arbitrary-A language and the printed Z/2 four-dimensional definitions leave an interpretation/generalization gap that must be resolved before an arbitrary-A theorem is stated.
A conjectural quadratic phase is an additional hypothesis beyond the conditional stable no-go argument.
